title: Lily Cleans Her Room
setting: A small, bright bedroom on a Sunday morning.

characters.name: Lily
characters.look: Lily (a seven-year-old girl with red hair in two pigtails and a yellow dress with white dots)

sentences.en: On Sunday, Lily cleans her small bedroom.
sentences.zh: 星期天，莉莉打扫她的小卧室。
sentences.scene_prompt: Lily (a seven-year-old girl with red hair in two pigtails and a yellow dress with white dots) holds a broom in a small, untidy bedroom, morning sun at the window.
sentences.draw_note: Shows Lily starting to clean her bedroom; the day Sunday can't be shown.
sentences.narration: Lily holds a broom in a small, untidy bedroom, morning sun at the window.

sentence_targets.en: A room used mainly for sleeping.
the day after Saturday and before Monday

sentences.en: She puts her clothes on the bed.
sentences.scene_prompt: Lily (a seven-year-old girl with red hair in two pigtails and a yellow dress with white dots) puts a pile of clothes on her bed.
sentences.narration: Lily puts a pile of clothes on her bed.

sentence_targets.en: items worn to cover the body
to move something into a particular place or position

sentences.en: One sock is on the left side.
sentences.scene_prompt: A single striped sock lies on the floor on the left side of the bed; Lily (a seven-year-old girl with red hair in two pigtails and a yellow dress with white dots) points at it.
sentences.narration: A single striped sock lies on the floor on the left side of the bed. Lily points at it.

sentence_targets.en: On the side opposite the right.
An edge or surface of something, or the space beside it.
a clothing item covering the foot and lower leg

sentences.en: Should she keep this pretty skirt or that?
sentences.zh: 她该留下这条漂亮的裙子，还是那条？
sentences.scene_prompt: Lily (a seven-year-old girl with red hair in two pigtails and a yellow dress with white dots) holds up two pretty skirts, a pink one in one hand and a blue one in the other, looking from one to the other.
sentences.draw_note: Shows Lily choosing between two skirts; the question 'should she keep' can't be shown exactly.
sentences.narration: Lily holds up two pretty skirts, a pink one in one hand and a blue one in the other, looking from one to the other.

sentence_targets.en: To continue having something rather than giving it away.
Clothing hanging from the waist, without separate sections for legs.
Attractive and pleasant to look at.
Used to connect alternatives or choices

sentences.en: The window glass is too dirty now.
sentences.scene_prompt: Lily (a seven-year-old girl with red hair in two pigtails and a yellow dress with white dots) frowns at a very dusty, smeared window pane.
sentences.narration: Lily frowns at a very dusty, smeared window pane.

sentence_targets.en: more than is wanted, needed, or suitable
A hard, usually transparent material used for windows and containers.

sentences.en: She cleans it once, and it shines.
sentences.zh: 她擦了一遍，窗户就亮了。
sentences.scene_prompt: Lily (a seven-year-old girl with red hair in two pigtails and a yellow dress with white dots) wipes the window with a cloth and the glass sparkles.
sentences.narration: Lily wipes the window with a cloth and the glass sparkles.

sentences.en: Then she sits down with some chips.
sentences.zh: 然后她拿着一些薯条坐下。
sentences.scene_prompt: Lily (a seven-year-old girl with red hair in two pigtails and a yellow dress with white dots) sits on the bed with a small bowl of chips.
sentences.narration: Lily sits on the bed with a small bowl of chips.

sentence_targets.en: fried potato strips in British English; thin slices in American English

sentences.en: A clean room gives her a good feeling.
sentences.zh: 干净的房间让她心情很好。
